subject: Clarify: DPA roles, subprocessor notify window, and breach playbook
messages:
From: Kelly Park <kelly@medsync.health>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — quick DPA questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier — the demo was helpful. A couple of items Legal needs clarified before we move to procurement:

- Can you confirm Redwood's position on controller vs processor in the hosted API and Dedicated deployment? We need to know what we are signing for (controller/processor responsibilities).
- What is Redwood's typical subprocessor notification window? We need an SLA on when we'll be notified if a subprocessor change or security incident involving a subprocessor happens.
- In a breach scenario impacting MedSync data, what is your incident notification playbook (timeline, evidence, point of contact)?
- Can you provide SOC 2 summary and confirm data residency options for EU vs US for our pilot?

If you can send a short written recap + current DPA and SOC2 summary, I can route to Legal. Ideally get back by EOD tomorrow — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Kelly Park
Head of IT & Security
MedSync Health

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — quick DPA questions

Hi Kelly — thanks for the note and great questions. Sending an initial written recap below and looping in Ben and Jordan from Sales & Privacy to confirm a couple of specifics. I attached our current DPA and SOC2 summary for Legal to review.

High-level answers (short):
- Controller vs Processor: Redwood is generally a processor for hosted API usage. For Dedicated or Private deployments we operate under the same Processor model but customers can request specific contractual language around data control in the Private deployment — happy to flag that to Legal.
- Subprocessor notification window: Our standard is to notify customers of subprocessor additions or changes via the customer console and email; for security incidents involving a subprocessor we follow the incident playbook (below) and will notify the customer according to the incident severity SLA. Jordan/Ben — please confirm the typical notify window we can commit to.
- Breach playbook: preliminary timeline included in this message. Full timeline and evidence package are provided on request.
- Data residency: We support region pinning on Dedicated and Redwood Private; hosted customers can request EU residency options — will confirm the region options available for a pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben/Jordan to confirm the subprocessor notify SLA (48/72 hours).
2) I’ll send a short summary of the incident notification playbook and what evidence we can provide (logs, audit trail, SOC2 report).
3) If you want DPA redlines, please route them to legal@medsync.health and we’ll have our contracts team prioritize.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf, SOC2_AuditSummary_2025.pdf

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference
(650) 555-0118

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — quick DPA questions

Vanessa — quick answers we can give now. I copied Marissa for product nuance on residency.

- Controller/Processor stance: Confirm Redwood operates as a Processor. We accept Limited Controller responsibilities only if specifically contracted and scoped for Private deployments. Standard hosted API customers are Processors only.

- Subprocessor notification window: Our baseline customer-facing commitment is 30 days for routine subprocessor additions; for security incidents involving a subprocessor we escalate and notify customers as soon as we confirm impact. Practically, for Tier 1 incidents we aim to notify within 48 hours of confirmation. For contractual asks we can consider 72-hour contract language if MedSync needs that SLA — we should flag to Legal.

- Breach playbook (short):
  * T+0: Detection and Triage (internal)
  * T+6 hours: Incident classification and initial customer-facing statement (if impact suspected)
  * T+24-48 hours: Confirmed impact — detailed notification with affected scope, timeline, temporary mitigations, and PoC
  * T+72 hours+: Evidence package (logs, change history, subprocessor timeline) delivered under secure transfer (SFTP/secure Drive)

- Evidence/Artifacts available: access logs (token-level), trace for request IDs, KV cache invalidation timestamps, audit log export (if on Dedicated / Private), SOC2 summary.

- Residency: Marissa — can you confirm EU-hosting options for a pilot (region pinning vs Dedicated)?

If Legal needs a 72-hour hard SLA for subprocessor-breach notify we can scope that but prefer 48 hours as operational target.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
